U.S. Department
of Transportation
Pipeline and Hazardous
Materials Safety

901 Locust Street, Suite 480
Kansas City, MO 64106

NOTICE OF PROBABLE VIOLATION
and
PROPOSED COMPLIANCE ORDER
VIA ELECTRONIC MAIL TO: jeff.ramsey@fhr.com; randy.lenz@fhr.com;
kelley.cabrerra@fhr.com; kim.gerold@fhr.com
December 30, 2024
Mr. Jeff Ramsey
President and CEO
Flint Hills Resources, LLC
4111 E. 37th Street North
Wichita, Kansas 67220
CPF 3-2024-028-NOPV
Dear Mr. Ramsey:
From April 18, 2022 through December 14, 2022, of the on-site inspection, representatives of the
Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Pipeline Safety
(OPS), and the Minnesota Office of Pipeline Safety (MNOPS), pursuant to Chapter 601 of 49
United States Code (U.S.C.), inspected the Wisconsin Refined Products Pipeline System, the
Wescott LPG System, and the Junction City LPG Pipeline System, located in Minnesota and
Wisconsin and operated by Flint Hills Resources, LC, and Flint Hills Resources Pine Bend, LLC
(collectively referred to as FHR).
As a result of the inspection, it is alleged that FHR has committed probable violations of the
Pipeline Safety Regulations, Title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). The items inspected,
and the probable violations are:
1.

§ 195.446 Control room management.
(a) . . . .
(c) Provide adequate information. Each operator must provide its controllers with
the information, tools, processes and procedures necessary for the controllers to
carry out the roles and responsibilities the operator has defined by performing
each of the following:

 (1) . . . .
(3) Test and verify an internal communication plan to provide adequate means for
manual operation of the pipeline safely, at least once each calendar year, but at
intervals not to exceed 15 months;
FHR failed to test and verify an internal communication plan to provide for adequate means for
manual operations to the pipeline safely at least once each calendar not to exceed 15 months for
calendar years 2019, 2020 and 2021, per the requirements of § 195.446(c)(3). Specifically, FHR
failed to provide an adequate means for safe manual operations of the pipeline and failed to
properly test and verify its internal communication plan. PHMSA's review of FHR’s records for
calendar years 2019, 2020, and 2021 revealed that FHR conducted a table-top drill simulating a
SCADA failure. However, the drill was limited in scope and did not demonstrate a valid means
of manually operating the pipeline in the event of a SCADA failure. Furthermore, PHMSA
determined from records of the drill that FHR’s internal communication plan and procedures for
manual operation were inadequate to ensure safe operations during such an event.
PHMSA reviewed FHR’s procedures, including PRC1490.120, PRC1490.123, PRC1490.225,
PRC1490.229, and PRC1490.238, and found they lacked provisions for testing and verifying
manual pipeline operation. This deficiency stemmed from FHR’s position that they do not
manually operate the pipeline (i.e., move product through the pipeline) once it is shut down. In
response to PHMSA’s Post-Inspection Written Preliminary Findings, FHR stated, “FHR's
procedures outline that during a SCADA failure/outage, the company will not operate the
pipeline systems manually and would shut down the pipeline systems.” Furthermore, FHR
asserted, “[i]n the event of a SCADA failure/outage, the operators of the pipeline facility are no
longer controllers in a control room. They are not operating a pipeline facility through a SCADA
system. §195.446 Control Room Management does not apply when there is a SCADA
failure/outage.”
PHMSA disagrees with FHR’s position because: (1) it does not align with a straightforward
application of the regulation for FHR to define the roles and responsibilities of its controllers to
comply with § 195.446(c)(3), and (2) a pipeline is in operational status as long as hazardous
material is contained in the pipeline system, and therefore an internal communication plan to
provide adequate means for manual operation of the pipeline safely is applicable to controllers
and control rooms in the event of SCADA failure/outage. 1
Accordingly, procedures for manual operation must be provided to controllers and other
operations personnel to ensure safety under all operating conditions, including during no-flow or
shutdown scenarios. These procedures must define roles and responsibilities for manual
operations, to comply with § 195.446(c)(3), and be integrated with FHR’s written procedures as
mandated by § 195.402(a).

1

See Control Room Management FAQs, PHMSA, at FAQ C.07, C.09, and C.14 (explaining that, in the event of
SCADA failure/outage, a communication plan for manual, safe operation of the pipeline is necessary, even if just to
bring it to shutdown status), https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/pipeline/control-room-management/control-roommanagement-faqs (Issued Jan. 16, 2018).

2

 As a result of FHR’s stated operating beliefs and practices, its procedures for testing and
verifying an internal communication plan for manual operations at least once each calendar year
(not exceeding 15 months) were found to be inadequate, and FHR failed to comply with
§ 195.446(c)(3).
2.

§ 195.505 Qualification program.
Each operator shall have and follow a written qualification program. The program
shall include provisions to:
(a) . . . .
(b) Ensure through evaluation that individuals performing covered tasks are
qualified;

FHR failed to ensure that an individual performing a covered task was qualified, per the
requirements of § 195.505(b). In response to PHMSA’s request for dig repair records, FHR
disclosed that after internally reviewing its repair records, it had found that on January 16, 2020,
two grind-out repairs (pipe defect removal by grinding) were completed by a contractor
individual who was not qualified to FHR’s Operator Qualification Program (OQ) Covered Task
1004, “Repair of Steel Pipe by Grinding." Therefore, FHR failed to ensure that individuals
performing covered tasks were qualified on two occasions, contrary to the requirements of
§ 195.505(b).
Proposed Compliance Order
With respect to Item 1, pursuant to 49 U.S.C. § 60118, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials
Safety Administration proposes to issue a Compliance Order to FHR. Please refer to the
Proposed Compliance Order, which is enclosed and made a part of this Notice.
Warning Item
With respect to Item 2, we have reviewed the circumstances and supporting documents involved
in this case and have decided not to conduct additional enforcement action or penalty assessment
proceedings at this time. We advise you to promptly correct this item. Failure to do so may result
in additional enforcement action.
Response to this Notice
Enclosed as part of this Notice is a document entitled Response Options for Pipeline Operators
in Enforcement Proceedings. Please refer to this document and note the response options. All
material you submit in response to this enforcement action may be made publicly available. If
you believe that any portion of your responsive material qualifies for confidential treatment
